<reason>B won the central IBR-equivalence clash. A argued discharge is just faster IBR without cruelty, but B showed timing matters: IBR rechecks yearly and collects if income rises while discharge locks in at the trough and lets borrower keep all future upside from a non-repossessable degree. A never solved irreversibility or strategic underemployment, and twice exceeded limits causing clipped speeches.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's trough-timing rebuttal that same low-income paperwork means different things under IBR vs discharge - IBR keeps loan alive to capture upside, discharge permanently severs it - which neutralized A's taxpayer-equivalence and turned waiting into the test.</best_rebuttal>
